## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pīṭhajātaka* (Ja 337) is a canonical birth story in the Pali *Jātaka* collection, rendered in English as *The Seat* [SuttaCentral]. In the edition of the *Jātaka* and its commentary edited by V. Fausböll, it appears as the seventh story in its section, opening with the canonical verse lemma *Na te pīṭhan ti* [Fausböll 1883].
According to its opening narrative framework (*nidāna*), the Buddha told this story while staying at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthi concerning a certain monk [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. Having arrived at Jetavana from the countryside, the monk put away his bowl and robes, paid homage to the Master, and inquired of the young novices which householders in Sāvatthi were supportive and hospitable to visiting monks [Fausböll 1883].
Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms that canonical verse portions of the text (notably segments §2.4–4.4) are aligned with and preserved in the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (§964–970) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan literature are recorded by either SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
